# AI use in this project

The SMAC steering committee confirmed on 31 August 2026 that AI use is permitted
for all parts of the competition. This file is therefore an engineering record,
not a confession: it exists so we can answer precisely when a judge asks who
wrote what.

## Session 1 — 10 September 2026

**Tool:** Claude (Opus 5), acting as implementer with Sulaiman directing.

**Generated by AI, unreviewed by a human at time of writing:**
- Every Swift file in `Jaddati/` (15 files, ~1,900 lines)
- `Jaddati.xcodeproj/project.pbxproj`, hand-written rather than Xcode-generated
- `spike/voice_spike.sh`
- This file, `README.md`, `docs/verified-vs-unverified.md`

**Checks the AI actually ran:**
- Brace, parenthesis and bracket balance across all 15 Swift files — all balanced
- Static review pass that caught and fixed three defects before handover:
  a Swift key path into a tuple (`ForEach(..., id: \.title)`), which does not
  compile; a stray non-view statement inside a `ViewBuilder`; and an unnecessary
  `@MainActor` isolation on two observable objects that risked concurrency errors
- Confirmed the ElevenLabs endpoint shapes against current official documentation
  rather than from memory

**Checks the AI could NOT run, and did not claim to:**
- Swift compilation — no toolchain was reachable from its environment
- Any execution on the simulator or on hardware
- Any live call to ElevenLabs — its network egress to `api.elevenlabs.io` was
  blocked, which is why the spike is a script for Sulaiman to run rather than a
  result

**Human review status:** not started. No one has yet read this code or built it.

## How to keep this file honest

Add a row when work happens. Never mark a human review complete without the
human saying so. Never describe a build as passing that no one has run.
